sentiment.rationale: Forward guidance was effectively reduced: the 2024 free cash flow outlook was lowered to 'low-single digit billions' from prior expectations, and the $10 billion free cash flow goal was pushed out to 'later in the 2025/2026 window.' The company explicitly slowed 737 production below 38 per month and expects it to remain there for the first half, with deliveries under pressure. Management language is cautious and focused on quality and safety actions, not growth. The structural risk from the Alaska Airlines accident and ongoing FAA oversight is significant and unresolved.

summary.revenue: $16.6 billion, down 8% versus the prior year, primarily reflecting lower 737 delivery volume.
summary.eps: GAAP loss per share of ($0.56) and core (non-GAAP) loss per share of ($1.13).
summary.guidance: 2024 free cash flow expected to be generation in the low-single digit billions, backend loaded. Second quarter free cash flow expected to be another sizable use of cash. $10 billion free cash flow goal pushed to later in the 2025/2026 window. 737 production will remain below 38 per month for the first half of the year, higher in the second half. 787 production will be below five per month for most of the year.
summary.margin: GAAP operating margin of (0.5)%, core (non-GAAP) operating margin of (2.3)%. Commercial Airplanes operating margin of (24.6)%. Defense, Space & Security operating margin of 2.2%. Global Services operating margin of 18.2%.
key_risks: Lower 737 deliveries and 737-9 grounding customer considerations impacting financial results.
Production slowdown below 38 per month on 737, with deliveries under pressure in the first half.
Ongoing FAA oversight and 90-day quality control plan, with no immediate rate increases.
Losses on fixed-price development programs in BDS ($222 million in the quarter).
Supply chain constraints on 787 (heat exchangers, seats).
Potential labor disruption from IAM negotiations over the summer.
Spirit AeroSystems acquisition discussions are complex and uncertain.
Cash balance declined significantly to $7.5 billion from $16.0 billion at the start of the quarter.
key_opportunities: Total company backlog grew to $529 billion, including over 5,600 commercial airplanes.
Strong demand across the portfolio, with 125 net orders for Commercial Airplanes in the quarter.
Defense, Space & Security backlog of $61 billion with $9 billion in orders in the quarter.
Global Services continues strong performance with 18.2% operating margin and 7% revenue growth.
Expectation to deliver most inventoried 737 and 787 airplanes by year-end, shutting down shadow factories.
BDS expected to return to high-single digit margins by 2025/2026 timeframe.

management_tone.label: cautious
management_tone.justification: Management repeatedly emphasizes the need to 'slow down,' 'take the time necessary,' and focus on 'stability' and 'quality' over growth, with explicit statements like 'we will take the time necessary to strengthen our quality and safety management systems' and 'we are not going to rush it.'
